citation: Puttonen J., Rantanen S., Laakso F., Kurjenniemi J., Aho K., Acar G. (2014) Satellite model for Network Simulator 3. SIMUTools.
description: SNS3 (Satellite Network Simulator 3) is a satellite network extension of the ns-3 platform. It models geostationary multi-spot-beam satellite systems with DVB-S2 forward links and DVB-RCS2 return links, including random access, demand-assigned multiple access, adaptive coding and modulation, link budgets with antenna patterns and rain fading, and handover; newer versions add low-Earth-orbit constellations with SGP4 satellite movement, inter-satellite link routing taken from Hypatia, and LoRaWAN over satellite. It was initially developed by Magister Solutions under a European Space Agency contract and is now maintained as open source, with release tags that follow ns-3 versions (the newest is 3.48). Coverage: user-defined satellite systems covering any region of the Earth, with reference scenarios over Europe. Format and access: C++ source on GitHub installed as an ns-3 contrib module; free of charge under the GNU GPL version 3. Caveats: configuration is complex; reference data files describe specific ESA scenarios; LEO support is newer and less validated than the GEO models. Simulation uses: capacity planning and network flow of satellite broadband and IoT backhaul, resilience of satellite links to rain fade and outages, and emergency communications via satellite. Related records: runs on ns-3, reuses Hypatia routing, and OpenSAND is an emulation alternative.
